hint: A grep whose pattern begins with .{0,N}, over a CLI binary (claude, grok, agy: 150-270 MB), tries a match at every byte and pegs a CPU for minutes.  Run `timeout 30 strings FILE | grep -F -i -m 20 'literal'`, or find the literal with Python's mmap.find and read the bytes around it.
catches: C=~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.308; LC_ALL=C grep -a -o ".\{0,160\}Jump to bottom.\{0,160\}" $C | head -5
for f in ~/.grok/downloads/grok-1.0.70-macos-aarch64 ~/.local/bin/agy; do timeout 60 grep -a -o -i '.{0,60}(jump to bottom|hooks).{0,60}' $f | head; done
